compendium_intro: Rites are performed at an <color=orange>obliterator</color>. Open it and click the rune stone on the flap under it to turn its rites on: until then it obliterates everything as usual. Put a rite item in, along with whatever else you want to be rid of, and pull the lever. When the thunder takes your sacrifice, the rite takes hold.
compendium_rules: One sacrifice performs every rite with enough of its item in. When two can't go together (two weather rites, say), the one from the lowest item goes first and the other's item is sacrificed for nothing. Performing a rite again starts its time over. Each rite going on shows as a status with the time left, and the book on the obliterator's flap opens the rites page, where clicking an item puts in as many as its rite needs.

compendium_group_atmospheric: The weather, for everyone, shown as each biome's own kind of it: snow in the mountains, Mistlands rain in the Mistlands, ash rain in the Ashlands. One weather rite at a time: a new one replaces the last. Raids, boss fights and dungeons keep their own weather, and a weather rite never makes a place warmer than its own weather would.
compendium_group_celestial: The sun and the wind, for everyone. Time itself goes on as usual: days are counted, crops grow, beds go by the real clock and clocks show the real time.
compendium_group_biome_mastery: One part of the world bent to your will, for everyone.
compendium_group_domain: Work within {0} m of the obliterator they were performed at, and their status shows only there. Each ends when its obliterator is destroyed. Only the Grounding Rite ends them, so nobody's growth or protection is ended by accident.
compendium_group_blessings: For the players standing within {0} m of the obliterator when its thunder strikes: its lightning strikes each of them, harmlessly. Each keeps their own, through logging out, until it ends or they die. No rite ends them early.
compendium_group_kinship: For everyone on the server at once, wherever they are. One sacrifice performs only one of them. Each player stops what they are doing to toast, roar, flex or cheer, and nobody can be hurt meanwhile (the Rally-Horn Rite instead offers a call each player may answer). Once a kinship rite gives a player something, no other one of the same rite can until the wait is over, even through death; a player it passes by gets no wait.
compendium_group_reckoning: Fights for great rewards, and the rites that end others.
compendium_clear: Clear skies: no rain, snow or fog, for building, farming and travelling. Cold biomes stay as cold as their own weather would make them. The Swamp keeps its own weather.

compendium_ragnarok:
A boss rush: {0} bosses rise at the obliterator one after another in a random order, {1} apart, picked among those every player within {2} m has slain, a different one each while there are enough. Every boss is as strong as the strongest boss they have all slain, with a star for each boss it was raised past (after Bonemass, Eikthyr is 2★ and the Elder 1★, both as strong as Bonemass): its health and damage are raised to match, and so are those of what it summons. Anyone who has slain Bonemass or a stronger boss counts Eikthyr and the Elder as slain too, so players who missed the early game aren't left out. Three different bosses must be defeated first: if nobody inside has slain Bonemass or a stronger boss, nothing rises and the key items go back into the obliterator. If no boss has fallen to everyone inside, nothing rises either. Which bosses come is only seen as each rises. The sky burns ember and gold and the area is marked on everyone's map.
A shield dome closes over its Blood Grounds like the Crimson Rite's: nobody gets in or out, bosses can't leave, no portal into or out of it works, nothing can be built, repaired or torn down inside, and no rite but the Sanctuary Rite can be performed there.
The bosses drop what they usually do, but no trophies. There is no time limit: slay them all and lightning strikes down a chest around the obliterator for each boss, one after another. Each holds resources of that boss's own lands (Eikthyr's the Meadows', the Elder's the Black Forest's...), picked at random from common, uncommon, rare and (for Eikthyr, the Queen and Fader) legendary ones, boss summoning items among them: early bosses give fewer kinds in bigger amounts, later ones more kinds. More of each for every star it had. It is split among a few containers of the boss's own lands: its dungeon chest (a Meadows chest for Eikthyr, a dvergr chest for the Queen...), then chests and barrels. A beam of light rises from each chest until it is first opened. Emptied, a chest vanishes, and broken it drops only its treasure. However it ends, the bosses and creatures still inside vanish and drop nothing. It breaks off with no reward if the obliterator is destroyed, everyone inside falls or leaves, or the Sanctuary Rite ends it. Only one Crimson, Ragnarök or Hoard-Bane Rite can go on at a time.
compendium_hoard_bane:
One of Hildir's minibosses comes for the chest sacrificed: Brenna (the brass chest) with skeletons, Geirrhafa (the silver chest) with ulvs, or Zil and Thungr (the bronze chest) with fulings, each harder than the last. It rises on the edge of a {0} m arena with four followers and hunts the players, under a shield that takes no damage. Every 30 seconds, while fewer than two followers stand, one more comes in where it is furthest from the players.
Three elites, each with its pack, wait in {1} m lairs evenly around the edge. They don't move and take no damage until a player steps into their lair or something hits one of them, and then the whole pack wakes: a hit from afar only wakes them, so no sneak attack. Lightning strikes the miniboss as each elite falls; with the last, its shield breaks.
The miniboss is stronger than usual, the stronger the strongest boss everyone inside has slain, but never as strong as that boss. It drops no chest nor trophy. A shield dome closes over the Blood Grounds like the Ragnarök Rite's: nobody gets in or out, no portal works, nothing can be built inside and only the Sanctuary Rite performed. There is no time limit: slay the miniboss and lightning strikes down a dungeon chest of the biome by the obliterator, which holds treasure: coins and valuables (the bronze chest's richest, then the silver's, then the brass's), and idols from every age up to the one everyone inside has reached: one from the top two ages, one from the two below, and so on, each a battle or a protection idol. Like the Ragnarök Rite's, the chest shines until first opened and vanishes once emptied. However it ends, what it brought vanishes and drops nothing. It breaks off with no reward if the obliterator is destroyed, everyone inside falls or leaves, or the Sanctuary Rite ends it.

A Reckoning rite needs room for its creatures: a dozen open spots for the Crimson Rite's raids, half a dozen for the Ragnarök Rite's bosses, and room for all of the Hoard-Bane Rite's lairs and miniboss; with less, it is refused.
